title: feat: fall back to Vertex global before AI Studio for gemini-fast
author: voodoohop
pr_body_excerpt:
- Adds `google/gemini-2.5-flash-lite:openrouter:vertex-global`, an OpenRouter route pinned to `google-vertex` (global), same price as the EU primary
- Declares it as the first fallback pair for `google/gemini-2.5-flash-lite` (`gemini-fast`); the existing AI Studio pair stays as the last resort
- Why: every "Gemini blocked the response: OTHER" 502 in Tinybird has `fallback_used=true`. Vertex EU 429s spill to AI Studio, which blocks 41% / 13% of the two heaviest keys' fallback calls. Vertex global has its own quota and the same safety behaviour, so the spill now stays on Vertex
- Only Google serves this model on OpenRouter (2 Vertex + 3 AI Studio endpoints), so this mirrors the Claude `:openrouter:vertex-global` pairs
- Updates the static fallback test and the enter effective-prices snapshot

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

gist.headline: Gemini finds another garden
gist.blurb: gemini-fast now checks Vertex global before asking AI Studio for a hand. Same model, another patch of quota, fewer conversations wandering into the weeds.
gist.summary: Added the OpenRouter route `google/gemini-2.5-flash-lite:openrouter:vertex-global` as gemini-fast’s first fallback, keeping Vertex EU 429 spillover on Google Vertex global before the existing AI Studio fallback.
gist.impact: Users of `google/gemini-2.5-flash-lite` get a more resilient fallback path with Vertex global’s independent quota and matching safety behavior, reducing reliance on AI Studio when Vertex EU is busy.
gist.visual_concept: Depict gemini-fast’s fallback routing as a cozy garden path: Polli guides glowing text-message pollen from a busy Vertex EU greenhouse to a second, open Vertex global greenhouse, while the AI Studio shed waits quietly farther down the path as the final backup. Use two friendly CRT route-sign monitors and sprouting code-plants to make independent capacity and orderly fallback priority visible.
